chain_status_rule: the weakest link, never an average

attested.means: the record was found and every check on it passed

blocked.means: a refusal stopped the replay before it could look

hash_verified.means: the stored payload hash equals a hash recomputed over the stored payload

legacy_gap.becomes_proof_when: never, for this record. The digest it referred to cannot be reconstructed and regenerating one would produce a different digest for the same period.
legacy_gap.means: the record predates the table that would have held it. It is not wrong, it was un-storable at the time.

linked_record_found.means: the record this one points at exists and is readable

missing_record.becomes_proof_when: the record is written by the path that owes it
missing_record.means: the record should exist and does not

not_attestable.means: this system cannot speak to it at all, in this scope. Production and legal standing are the usual subjects.

not_attributable.becomes_proof_when: an actor or source is recorded at write time
not_attributable.means: nothing records who or what this came from

not_replayable.becomes_proof_when: the capability is activated and the event occurs
not_replayable.means: the event did not happen, so there is nothing to replay - a delivery that was never sent has no delivery to attest

unknown.becomes_proof_when: somebody determines it. An unknown link proves nothing and is ranked below every gap so a chain cannot read green through one.

why: every one of the 85 delivery intents has an audit link that resolves and a digest link that never will. One status per record would have to pick one and be wrong about the other.
